rules.title: Source package resolution precedes binary archive resolution
rules.statement: A `use pkg;` import resolves `pkg` by first consulting the source (text) package index built from `.logos` files; only if no source package declares `pkg` is the binary archive index consulted. If neither supplies `pkg`, compilation fails with a 'cannot find package' error.

rules.title: `use pkg from <M>` pins resolution to module M's archive
rules.statement: An import `use pkg from <M>;` resolves `pkg` from the archive whose embedded module canonical-name is `M`, independent of which other archive(s) also provide a package named `pkg`. This lets two distinct modules supplying a same-named package coexist; a bare `use pkg;` and `use pkg from M;` are keyed independently and both load.
rules.divergence: Logos addition (`from <module>` import selector); no Rust equivalent.

rules.title: `from <M>` with unknown module name falls through to default resolution
rules.statement: If `use pkg from <M>;` names a module `M` for which no loaded archive is registered, resolution falls through to the default text-then-binary path; the precise 'no loaded module' diagnostic is emitted by later semantic analysis rather than the loader.
rules.uncertainty: Loader behavior only; the actual error is emitted in a separate sema unit.

rules.title: Each package loaded at most once; files deduplicated by canonical path
rules.statement: A package is loaded at most once per build (keyed by package name, or by (module,package) under a `from` import); within a load each file is added at most once, identified by its canonical filesystem path.

rules.title: Imported packages are loaded before their importer (post-order)
rules.statement: Package dependencies declared via `use` are loaded depth-first in post-order, so a package's transitive imports are emitted before the package itself; the final module sequence is additionally topologically sorted to make dependency-first ordering uniform across source and binary loads.

rules.title: A `.logos` file is importable only if it declares a package
rules.statement: Only `.logos` files carrying a `package` declaration are indexed and thus reachable via `use`; a file with no package declaration is silently skipped and cannot be imported by name.

rules.title: Cross-cutting foundation packages auto-load without explicit `use`
rules.statement: Foundation packages under prefixes `std.lang`, `std.writ`, or `logos.lang` (excluding the `logos.lang.writ` substrate) are implicitly available to every compilation: when an archive is loaded for a requested package, sibling packages with these prefixes are also loaded so cross-cutting traits and types (Default, Ord, Send, Clone, etc.) resolve without an explicit import edge.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: implicit prelude is prefix-scoped to the lang tier (transitional; manifest-tier system intended).
rules.uncertainty: Exact prefix set is a transitional heuristic per source comments.

rules.title: A prelude sibling already supplied by source is not re-loaded from binary
rules.statement: An auto-loaded prelude sibling package is skipped when the source (text) index already provides that package, preventing the same package's items/impls from being registered twice (which would otherwise produce duplicate-definition / conflicting-impl errors). The explicitly requested package is always loaded.

rules.title: Binary archive ABI compatibility is one-directional within a major version
rules.statement: A compiler may consume a binary library iff (a) the library's language major version equals the compiler's, and (b) for stable releases the library's minor version is <= the compiler's minor. A differing major is incompatible; a library built by a newer minor is rejected. An ABI-incompatible archive is not indexed (its packages become unavailable). Identical version strings are always compatible; legacy archives without a version stamp are not enforced.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: semantic-version ABI gate on binary modules (Rust has no stable cross-version library ABI).

rules.title: Pre-release / snapshot builds require exact version match
rules.statement: If either the library or the compiler is a pre-release (`-pre`) or snapshot (`+meta`) build, no ABI guarantee holds: only an exact version-string match is silently accepted; any mismatch is permitted but warned. The check is disabled entirely by environment override.

rules.title: Identifiers are ASCII-only
rules.statement: Identifiers consist of ASCII bytes only; a source line containing a non-ASCII (high-bit, >= 0x80) byte at the point of a syntax error is diagnosed as an identifier encoding error, since non-ASCII bytes cannot form a valid identifier token.
rules.divergence: A: diverges from Rust, which accepts Unicode (XID) identifiers.

rules.title: A binary archive carries a single owning module identity
rules.statement: Each binary archive declares at most one owning module via its embedded index header, giving a canonical module name and a mangling id; this identity is stamped onto every item decoded from the archive and is used downstream to qualify the items' symbols.
